trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This platinum is the reward for the other 54 trophies, so there is no separate task to complete: it unlocks automatically the moment your 54th trophy pops, whatever that trophy happens to be. Treat it as a planning trophy rather than a grind trophy. The run that earns it is roughly 200 hours long, and the only way to lose it is to miss the single missable trophy, Positive Mental Attitude, whose Chapter 1 meditation spot disappears for good once that chapter ends. Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter, clear the stranger strands and collectibles as you go, and save the long counters — 250 stunts, the shooting-range golds, and the 100% completion checklist — for the cleanup phase. When A Long Road, the 100% trophy, finally pops, this platinum pops right beside it, and the whole list is yours.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order; this one pops with the 54th.
Protect the run first: make a manual save at the start of every chapter.
Clear stranger strands, collectibles and activities during the story, not after it.
Leave the long counters (250 stunts, range golds, 100%) for the cleanup phase.
Finish A Long Road last — the platinum unlocks the moment it does.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission of Grand Theft Auto VI, so this trophy is unmissable and should be one of the first you ever earn. Play through the introduction as directed: the mission teaches the basic movement, driving and interaction controls while it sets up Lucia and Jason's story, and it ends on its own once the final objective is complete. There is nothing to prepare, no collectible to grab first, and no way to fail it permanently — if a section goes wrong, the game restarts you at the last checkpoint. The one habit worth starting here is manual saving: the game has no mission replay and no New Game Plus, so make a manual save the moment Chapter 1 opens. That single save protects you later, when the missable meditation trophy comes into play.
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission Gone Fishing.
Follow the on-screen objectives; the mission ends on its own.
If a section fails, retry from the checkpoint — progress is kept.
Make a manual save as soon as Chapter 1 opens, before anything else.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Paradise Lost unlocks when you finish the last mission of Chapter 1, and like every chapter trophy it is unmissable as long as you keep playing the story. Chapter 1 introduces Leonida, both protagonists, and the systems you will use for the rest of the game, so take your time with it rather than rushing the missions. Before the chapter ends, do the one thing in the game that can never be repeated: meditate at Lucia's balcony. That spot counts toward Positive Mental Attitude, the list's only missable trophy, and it vanishes once Chapter 1 closes. Make a manual save at the start of the chapter and another right before its final mission, so you always have a way back if you forget the balcony.
steps: Play through Chapter 1's missions in story order.
Before the chapter ends, meditate at Lucia's balcony (missable trophy progress).
Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 1 and before its final mission.
Finish the last mission of Chapter 1; the trophy pops at the chapter card.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: This trophy unlocks when you complete Chapter 2, and from here the game opens up properly: both protagonists are playable, and most of the trophy list becomes available for the first time. Chapter 2's missions are longer and introduce the crew, the heist planning, and the side systems that feed the activity and crime trophies later, so expect a step up in difficulty from Chapter 1 without anything that should stop a careful player. Use this chapter to start the habits that pay off across the whole list: try an activity type whenever you pass one, note the meditation spots you find, and keep a manual save at the start of the chapter. Nothing in Chapter 2 is missable on its own, but the saves you make here are your insurance for the finale.
steps: Play through Chapter 2's missions in story order.
Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 2.
Try any activity you pass (races, fishing, arcade) to start Master of None.
Note meditation spots you find for the missable trophy.
Finish the last mission of Chapter 2; the trophy pops at the chapter card.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Vice City, Baby! unlocks when you complete Chapter 3, and it marks the point where the robbery trophies start to open up in earnest. The missions in this chapter push you deeper into Vice City itself, and the free-roam crime systems — shop robberies, armored trucks, and the wanted-level play that feeds Hot Together and Retail Therapy — become practical to attempt between missions. Keep your manual-save habit: one save at the start of the chapter, and another before any mission that looks like a point of no return. Between missions, start the low-effort counters that run all game: discover new vehicles for Whip It Good, try a stunt jump when you see one, and keep an eye out for meditation spots and collectible cards.
steps: Play through Chapter 3's missions in story order.
Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 3.
Between missions, try a shop robbery or armored truck in free roam.
Discover new vehicles and attempt stunt jumps as you travel.
Finish the last mission of Chapter 3; the trophy pops at the chapter card.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Top Of The World, Ma unlocks when you complete Chapter 4, and by now you are deep into the story with most of the map and most of the side systems open. Chapter 4's missions are among the most demanding so far, and the bank-vault robberies that feed Maximum Withdrawal unlock in these later chapters, so start planning your escape routes before you attempt them rather than improvising under a wanted level. This is also a good chapter to sweep up the stranger strands you have been postponing: finishing any eight of them earns Strangers & Freaks, and several strands end in this stretch of the game. Keep the manual save at the chapter start, and keep the finale save discipline in mind — the final mission is coming, and there is no mission replay to fall back on.
steps: Play through Chapter 4's missions in story order.
Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 4.
Attempt a bank-vault robbery, planning the escape route first.
Finish any stranger strands you have left open (8 strands earn a silver).
Finish the last mission of Chapter 4; the trophy pops at the chapter card.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: This gold trophy unlocks when you complete the final mission of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is the story's natural endpoint — unmissable if you finish the game, but the one mission you should never walk into unprepared. The game has no mission replay and no New Game Plus, so the reported advice from trophy hunters is simple: make a manual save before you start the finale, and keep it. That save is your only way back to the story's closing stretch, whether you want to rewatch the ending, clean up a choice, or recover from a missed meditation spot in the final chapters. The mission itself is long and demanding, so stock up on armor, ammunition and snacks first, then play it through to the credits. When the mission ends, the gold pops and the cleanup phase of your platinum run begins.
steps: Make a manual save before starting the final mission — and keep it.
Stock up on armor, ammunition and supplies before the mission.
Play the final mission through to the credits.
If a story choice matters to you, your pre-finale save is the only way back.
The gold pops when the final mission completes.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Trust unlocks when you complete the story mission Breakfast Run, and like every named story mission on this list it is unmissable: play the story in order and it will come to you. Breakfast Run is a mid-game mission that leans on driving and timing rather than raw firepower, so bring a fast, sturdy car and pay attention to the route the mission sets out for you. If a section goes wrong, the checkpoint system restarts you close to where you failed, so a wipe costs minutes rather than the whole mission. There is no preparation that meaningfully changes the mission, and no collectible or side objective tied to it — just play it, finish it, and the trophy pops at the mission's end card.
steps: Progress the story until Breakfast Run appears in the mission list.
Bring a fast, sturdy car if the mission lets you choose your vehicle.
Follow the mission route and objectives as they appear.
Retry from checkpoints if a section fails; the trophy pops at the end card.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Break the Bank unlocks when you complete The Cartel Heist, one of the story's set-piece heist missions. Heists in this game are multi-stage affairs: a setup phase, the job itself, and usually a getaway under pressure, so go in with full armor and a weapon loadout you trust, and listen to the crew's callouts during the escape — they usually mark the safest route out. The mission is unmissable and appears as part of the story, so the only way to fail it is to quit the game mid-mission and never return. If you go down, checkpoints restart you at the start of the current stage rather than the whole heist. Finish the getaway, reach the end card, and the trophy pops.
steps: Progress the story until The Cartel Heist appears.
Stock full armor and a trusted weapon loadout before starting.
Follow the crew's callouts during the setup and the job.
During the getaway, follow the marked escape route instead of improvising.
Reach the mission end card; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Family Matters unlocks when you complete the story mission Child's Play, and it is unmissable — the mission arrives in story order and the trophy pops at its end card. Child's Play is a character-driven mission that mixes driving with a short combat section, so the preparation is light: make sure you have armor and a mid-range weapon before you start, and keep a car nearby for the driving stretch. The mission does not hide any trophy-relevant secret, and there is no alternate outcome that changes the unlock, so play it straight and enjoy the scene. If you fail a section, the checkpoint restart puts you back a minute or two at most. Finish the mission and the trophy is yours.
steps: Progress the story until Child's Play appears.
Bring armor and a mid-range weapon before starting.
Play the driving and combat sections as directed.
Retry from checkpoints if a section fails.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the end card.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: DWNFALL unlocks when you complete the story mission Headliners, and it is unmissable in the same way as every other named story mission: it arrives in story order and pops at the mission's end card. Headliners is a louder mission than most, with a sustained combat stretch that rewards cover discipline and headshots over rushing in, so bring armor, a rifle you are comfortable with, and plenty of ammunition. The game checkpoints generously inside missions, so a failed push restarts you at the start of the current firefight rather than the mission's beginning. There is no side objective that affects the trophy and no way to lock yourself out of it. Play the mission through, survive the finale of the fight, and DWNFALL is yours.
steps: Progress the story until Headliners appears.
Bring full armor, a rifle, and plenty of ammunition.
Use cover and headshots in the combat stretch; do not rush.
Retry from checkpoints if a firefight goes wrong.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the end card.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Hi-Jacked unlocks when you complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport, and it is unmissable like the rest of the story missions. Expect a mix of driving, stealth, and combat: the airport setting means long sightlines and open tarmac, so use cover, move between the parked aircraft and service vehicles, and watch for enemies flanking from the terminal side. Stock armor and a versatile weapon loadout before you start, and remember that checkpoints restart you at the current stage if a push fails. The mission's airport setting also doubles as a preview of Catch Me If You Can, the free-roam trophy for an unscheduled departure at VCIA — once you know the layout from this mission, that trophy is much easier to attempt later.
steps: Progress the story until VCIA Takedown appears.
Bring full armor and a versatile weapon loadout.
Use aircraft and service vehicles as cover on the open tarmac.
Watch for enemies flanking from the terminal side.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the end card.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Snow Storm unlocks when you complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory, a late-game mission with heavy combat, and it is unmissable. This is one of the tougher story missions on the list: the enemy count is high, the firefights are sustained, and the mission punishes players who stand in the open. Go in with full armor, a rifle with a scope if you have one, and the best ammunition you can buy, and advance from cover to cover rather than sprinting between objectives. Combat Focus is your friend here — it slows time and lets you pick targets cleanly. Checkpoints restart you at the current stage after a failure, so a wipe is a setback of minutes, not of the whole mission. Finish it and Snow Storm pops.
steps: Progress the story until Operation Savage Glory appears.
Bring full armor, a scoped rifle, and maximum ammunition.
Advance from cover to cover; never stand in the open.
Use Combat Focus to pick targets cleanly in heavy firefights.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the end card.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: A Long Road is the gold trophy for attaining 100% completion, and it is the last grind before the platinum — the platinum pops the moment this one does. The in-game completion checklist is reported as 35 tasks by Output Lag, covering the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles, the activities, and the stunt counters, and the game tracks each of them in its stats menu, so you can always see exactly what is left. The smart way to earn it is to treat it as a cleanup list rather than a second playthrough: finish the story, then work the checklist top to bottom, saving the long counters — 250 stunts and the shooting-range golds — for last, when free roam is all that remains. Nothing on the checklist is missable except the single meditation spot in Chapter 1, which is why the manual saves from phase one matter so much.
steps: Finish the story first; most checklist tasks complete themselves along the way.
Open the in-game completion stats to see the 35 reported tasks and what is left.
Work the list top to bottom: strangers, collectibles, activities, stunts.
Save the long counters (250 stunts, range golds) for the free-roam cleanup.
Reach 100%; the gold pops — and the platinum pops with it.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Cunning Stunts is the silver trophy for completing 250 stunts, and it is a pure counter trophy: the game counts every stunt you pull off, from the first jump in the story to the last near miss in free roam, and the total carries across the whole playthrough. Stunts include stunt jumps, near misses with traffic, airtime, and drifts, so the fastest way to build the count is to drive fast and close in free roam — weave through traffic on the highways for near misses, hit the marked stunt jumps you find, and take ramps and hills at speed for airtime. Do not grind it early: play the story naturally and the counter will climb on its own, then finish it in the cleanup phase with a fast car on a highway loop. Track the count in the stats menu and stop guessing.
steps: Let the counter build naturally during the story — do not grind it early.
Weave through highway traffic for near misses; hit stunt jumps and ramps.
Check the stunt count in the stats menu to see what is left.
In the cleanup phase, loop a highway in a fast car for near misses.
Reach 250 stunts; the silver pops.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Master of None asks you to try each type of activity once — a try, not a win, which makes it one of the friendliest trophies on the list. The activity types are the side systems scattered across Leonida: races, fishing, the arcade, the shooting range, bowling, meditation, hunting, and drone races. You do not need to win, score well, or finish first in any of them; starting one and playing it through is enough for it to count. The best time to earn it is during the story, whenever you pass an activity marker: duck into the arcade for one game, try one fishing spot, attempt one race. If you leave it to the cleanup phase, the activity locations are all marked on the map, and you can sweep the whole set in a couple of hours.
steps: Find any activity marker on the map: race, fishing, arcade, range, bowling, meditation, hunting, or drone race.
Start the activity and play it through once — a try counts, not a win.
Repeat for each activity type you have not tried yet.
Check the stats or activity menu to confirm which types are done.
Try the last remaining type; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shootist is the silver trophy for earning a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges, reported as 42 challenges by the eso.jffk trophy round-up, and it is one of the most demanding skill trophies on the list. Each challenge is a timed shooting trial with its own weapon, target layout, and gold threshold, so the way to earn it is to learn each challenge separately rather than brute-forcing them all in one session. Play a challenge, note the gold threshold and where you lose time, then repeat it until the pattern clicks — most challenges fall to a few focused attempts once you know the target order. Use the weapon the challenge gives you, keep your aim steady rather than fast, and take breaks between challenges to keep your aim fresh. Gold them all and the silver pops.
steps: Visit a shooting range and open the challenge list (42 reported challenges).
Attempt each challenge once to learn its gold threshold and target layout.
Repeat a challenge in focused attempts until the target order clicks.
Keep aim steady rather than fast; take breaks between challenges.
Gold the final challenge; the silver pops.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun asks you to win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location, and it is a course-knowledge trophy: the drones handle the same everywhere, but each course has its own gates, turns, and shortcuts, so the first attempt at a new location is usually a scouting run. Fly the course once to learn the gate order and where the tight turns are, then race it properly on the second attempt, cutting corners where the gates allow and boosting on the straights. The races are scattered across Leonida, so work them district by district rather than criss-crossing the map, and keep a note of which locations you have already won. Win the last location and the trophy pops.
steps: Find a Top Fun Drone Race location on the map.
Fly the course once as a scouting run to learn the gates and turns.
Race it properly on the next attempt, boosting on straights and cutting corners.
Work the locations district by district; note each win.
Win the final location; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Earn Cash, Not Kudos asks you to win 20 different races, and the word different is the whole trick: each race event counts once, so repeating the same easy race twenty times earns you nothing. Leonida's race calendar covers street races, off-road races, and the drone races, and the best approach is to sweep them in order of difficulty, starting with the short street circuits where a good car and clean cornering are enough to win. Bring the fastest car you own to each race, learn the course on a first attempt if you have to, and remember that winning is what counts — second place is a wasted run. Twenty wins sounds like a lot, but the races are short, and the counter climbs quickly once you find the events that suit your driving.
steps: Open the race list and pick an event you have not won yet.
Bring your fastest car and learn the course on a first attempt if needed.
Win the race — only wins count, and each event counts once.
Move to the next unwon event; sweep short street circuits first.
Win your 20th different race; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Baited My Tackle asks you to beat Cal in a fishing challenge, and the fight is won with steady reeling rather than speed. Fishing challenges in this game are a rhythm game: cast, wait for the bite, then reel with a steady hand, easing off when the line strains and pulling hard when the fish runs slack. Cal is a named rival, so expect him to post a strong score — the trick is not to rush. Watch the line tension the whole time, never let it snap, and keep your reeling smooth instead of mashing the button. If you lose, the challenge can be retried immediately, so a failed attempt costs you minutes. Beat Cal's score and the trophy pops.
steps: Find a fishing challenge where Cal is the rival.
Cast and wait for the bite; do not reel early.
Reel steadily, easing off when the line strains.
Never let the line snap; retry immediately if you lose.
Beat Cal's score; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Stick Fiddler asks you to complete an arcade game — any cabinet, any game, one full playthrough — and it is one of the easiest trophies on the list. The arcade cabinets are scattered across Leonida, usually in bars, arcades, and entertainment spots, and each one runs a short self-contained game. Pick the cabinet whose game looks simplest to you, play it through to its end screen, and the trophy pops. You do not need a high score, and you do not need to beat anyone: finishing is the whole requirement. If a game proves frustrating, walk away and try a different cabinet — any completed game counts. It is a good trophy to grab during the story whenever you pass an arcade, and it also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet in a bar or entertainment spot.
Pick the game that looks simplest and start it.
Play the game through to its end screen — finishing is enough.
If a game frustrates you, try a different cabinet instead.
Complete any arcade game; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Road to Rehabilitation unlocks when you complete the final mission for Andy, one of the stranger mission strands scattered across Leonida. Stranger strands are chains of side missions for named characters, and each one ends with a finale mission that carries its own trophy — Andy's strand is one of them. To reach it, find Andy's first mission marker on the map, play through each mission in his chain as it unlocks, and keep an eye on the strand tracker so you know how far along you are. The finale is a normal mission in difficulty, so bring armor and a decent weapon as a matter of habit. Finish Andy's last mission and the trophy pops, and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks, the silver for completing any eight strands.
steps: Find Andy's first stranger mission marker on the map.
Play each mission in Andy's chain as it unlocks.
Check the strand tracker to see how many missions remain.
Bring armor and a decent weapon to the finale.
Complete Andy's final mission; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: This Was No Boat Accident unlocks when you complete the final mission for Kenton, another of the stranger strands, and the name gives away the setting: expect boats, water, and a finale on or near the coast. Start Kenton's chain at his first mission marker, play each mission as it unlocks, and save a boat or a fast car nearby before the finale so the getaway is painless. The strand missions are self-contained and none of them is missable — if you leave Kenton alone for ten chapters, his chain will still be waiting when you come back. That makes the stranger trophies ideal filler between story chapters. Finish Kenton's last mission and the trophy pops, and the strand counts toward the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks.
steps: Find Kenton's first stranger mission marker on the map.
Play each mission in Kenton's chain as it unlocks.
Keep a boat or fast car nearby before the finale.
Play the finale; retry from checkpoints if a section fails.
Complete Kenton's final mission; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: The Lone Rider unlocks when you complete the final mission for Billy, one of the stranger strands, and the title points at a solo ride — expect a mission built around a single bike or a long drive rather than a crew job. Find Billy's first marker, play his chain mission by mission, and keep a good bike in your garage before the finale so you are not scrambling for transport mid-mission. Like every stranger strand, Billy's chain never expires: it waits patiently while you play the story, so there is no pressure to finish it the moment it appears. Work it between chapters when you want a change of pace. Finish Billy's last mission and the trophy pops, and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
steps: Find Billy's first stranger mission marker on the map.
Play each mission in Billy's chain as it unlocks.
Keep a good bike in your garage before the finale.
Play the finale; use checkpoints if a section fails.
Complete Billy's final mission; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers & Freaks is the silver trophy for completing any eight stranger mission strands across Leonida, and it is a volume trophy rather than a skill trophy: no single strand is hard, but eight of them take time. The stranger strands are the side-mission chains for characters like Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, and Tyrone, each ending in a finale mission with its own trophy, and the game marks their starting points on the map. The efficient route is to finish the five strands that carry their own trophies first, then pick three more of the shortest chains you can find — the strand tracker shows how many missions each chain has left. Work them between story chapters, one chain at a time, and the eighth finale pops the silver.
steps: Finish the five trophy strands first: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone.
Check the strand tracker for other chains and their remaining missions.
Pick the three shortest remaining chains and finish them.
Work one chain at a time between story chapters.
Complete your eighth strand; the silver pops.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Supply & Demand unlocks when you complete the final mission for Randy, one of the stranger strands, and the name points at a supply-run finale — expect a delivery or pickup under pressure, with a vehicle you need to keep in one piece. Find Randy's first marker, play his chain as the missions unlock, and before the finale make sure you have a sturdy vehicle and full armor, because a supply run gone wrong usually means a chase. Randy's chain never expires, so you can leave it and come back chapters later without losing anything. Finish the finale, deliver whatever needs delivering, and the trophy pops — and the strand counts toward the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks.
steps: Find Randy's first stranger mission marker on the map.
Play each mission in Randy's chain as it unlocks.
Before the finale, secure a sturdy vehicle and full armor.
Protect the cargo or vehicle during the finale run.
Complete Randy's final mission; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Spin On This! unlocks when you complete the final mission for Tyrone, the last of the five stranger strands with its own trophy, and the name hints at a spin — a turn, a record, or a getaway that goes sideways. Find Tyrone's first marker, play his chain mission by mission, and treat the finale like any other stranger finale: bring armor, a reliable weapon, and a fast car, and let the checkpoints absorb your mistakes. Tyrone's strand is self-contained and never expires, so there is no rush to finish it the moment it appears — slot it in between story chapters when you want a break from the main plot. Finish his last mission and the trophy pops, and with the other four trophy strands done you are five of the eight strands toward Strangers & Freaks.
steps: Find Tyrone's first stranger mission marker on the map.
Play each mission in Tyrone's chain as it unlocks.
Bring armor, a reliable weapon, and a fast car to the finale.
Play the finale; retry from checkpoints if a section fails.
Complete Tyrone's final mission; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Positive Mental Attitude is the only missable trophy on the whole list, and it is the trophy this entire guide is built around protecting. The task is simple — meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida, reported as 18 spots — but one of them, Lucia's balcony, exists only during Chapter 1 and vanishes when that chapter ends. There is no mission replay and no New Game Plus, so missing the balcony means starting a new save from scratch. The defense is a habit, not a skill: make a manual save at the start of every chapter, meditate at Lucia's balcony before Chapter 1 ends, and meditate at every spot you find as you travel, rather than saving them all for the cleanup phase. The meditation spots themselves are calm, scenic places marked in the world — the danger is never the meditation, it is forgetting to do it in time.
steps: Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 1 — before anything else.
Meditate at Lucia's balcony before Chapter 1 ends; it never comes back.
Meditate at every spot you find as you travel; do not save them for later.
Make a manual save at the start of every chapter, every time.
Meditate at the final spot; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Fair Game asks you to hunt a unique animal for Bret, and it plays out as a stranger strand with a hunting finale: follow Bret's chain to the hunt, then track the animal itself. Hunting in this game is a patience exercise — move slowly, watch the wind and the animal's tracks, and take the shot only when you have a clean line, because a spooked animal can cost you the whole attempt. Bring a scoped rifle and plenty of patience, and use the tracking clues the game gives you rather than wandering the hunting grounds at random. The animal is unique, so there is exactly one of it, and Bret's strand tells you where to look. Follow the strand, find the animal, make the shot, and the trophy pops.
steps: Find Bret's stranger strand and play it until the hunt is offered.
Bring a scoped rifle and head to the hunting grounds Bret points to.
Follow the tracks and clues; move slowly and watch the wind.
Take the shot only with a clean line — a spooked animal costs the attempt.
Bring down the unique animal; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Don't Touch My Deck is the silver trophy for completing three collectible card sets, and it is a scavenger hunt across Leonida: the cards are hidden in the world — tucked into shops, alleys, rooftops, and quiet corners — and each set is a group of cards that belong together. The collectibles menu tracks which cards you have and which sets are still open, so the first thing to do is open that menu and see what you already hold from playing the story. Then work district by district, sweeping one area at a time rather than chasing single cards across the map, and use the in-game hints for the cards that refuse to turn up. Three complete sets is the target, not every card in the game, so stop at three unless you are chasing 100% completion anyway.
steps: Open the collectibles menu to see which cards and sets you already hold.
Work district by district, sweeping one area at a time.
Check rooftops, alleys, and shop interiors for hidden cards.
Use the in-game hints for the last few cards of a set.
Complete your third set; the silver pops.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: You WAiNKer! is the silver trophy for using WAiNK It at 100 locations, and it is a pure coverage grind: the action itself is quick, but there are a hundred spots to visit. WAiNK It is the game's photo or check-in action at scenic and notable locations, and each location counts once, so the counter only moves when you visit somewhere new. The efficient route is to work district by district, sweeping each area's WAiNK spots before moving on, and to fold the visits into your other travel — hit a WAiNK spot whenever you pass one during the story or a collectible sweep. The map and the in-game tracker show which locations are done, so you are never guessing. Reach 100 and the silver pops.
steps: Learn the WAiNK It action and try it at one location to confirm it counts.
Work district by district, sweeping each area's spots before moving on.
Hit WAiNK spots whenever you pass one during story or collectible travel.
Check the tracker to see which districts still have unvisited spots.
WAiNK It at your 100th location; the silver pops.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: One Last Thing asks you to complete 50 challenges from the game's side-objective list, and the list is long enough that you can pick the easy ones first. Challenges are small, self-contained objectives scattered through the game — a stunt here, a trick shot there, a driving feat somewhere else — and the challenge menu shows the full list with your progress on each. The smart route is to open that menu early, star the challenges that look quick, and knock them out as you play: many complete themselves during normal story and free-roam play if you know they exist. Do not save them all for the end; a challenge you attempt while passing through an area is free, while a challenge you return for later costs a whole trip. Finish your fiftieth and the trophy pops.
steps: Open the challenge menu and read the full side-objective list.
Star the challenges that look quick and complete themselves during play.
Knock out challenges as you pass through their areas; do not backtrack for them.
Check the menu regularly to see how many of the 50 are done.
Complete your 50th challenge; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Hot Together asks you to lose a four-star wanted level with your partner beside you and escape the heat, and the partner requirement is what makes it tricky: you need your partner in the car or on foot with you when the heat dies down. Start by picking up your partner, then build the wanted level to four stars — robbing a shop or taking down police vehicles in a busy area gets you there quickly — and then break line of sight. The escape is about distance and hiding, not speed: duck into an alley or a parking garage, stay out of the police cones of vision, and wait for the stars to blink and fade while your partner stays close. If your partner wanders off or gets arrested, the attempt fails, so keep the escape short and stay together.
steps: Pick up your partner and keep them with you for the whole attempt.
Build a four-star wanted level in a busy area (robbery, police takedowns).
Break line of sight: duck into an alley or parking garage.
Stay hidden and out of the police vision cones until the stars fade.
Lose the wanted level with your partner beside you; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Retail Therapy asks you to rob three shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level, and the planning matters more than the robbing: you need three shops close together, a getaway car parked nearby, and a route you have already scouted. Pick a strip with three small shops in a row, park your car at the far end, and rob them in order, moving fast and keeping your partner with you. The wanted level must stay active through all three robberies — if it fades between shops, the chain breaks and you start over — so do not stop to fight the police or loot slowly. Keep moving, keep your partner close, and finish the third shop while the heat is still on. The trophy pops the moment the third robbery completes.
steps: Scout a strip with three small shops close together.
Park a getaway car at the far end of the strip.
Rob the shops in order with your partner beside you, moving fast.
Keep the wanted level active through all three robberies.
Finish the third shop while the heat is still on; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Whip It Good asks you to discover 100 vehicles, and each new model counts once — driving the same car a hundred times earns you nothing, but sitting in a hundred different models does. The collection log tracks which vehicles you have discovered, so open it early and see how far the story alone has taken you: mission vehicles, traffic, and parked cars all count the moment you get in one. The grind is really a sightseeing tour: different districts spawn different traffic, so drive through the rich neighborhoods for sports cars, the industrial areas for trucks, and the countryside for off-roaders and tractors. Whenever you see a model you have not driven, get in it — even a ten-second drive counts. Reach 100 models and the trophy pops.
steps: Open the vehicle collection log to see which models you already own.
Drive through varied districts: rich areas, industrial zones, countryside.
Get into any model you have not driven yet, even for ten seconds.
Check the log regularly for the models you are still missing.
Discover your 100th vehicle; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Gunslinger asks you to take down five enemies in a single use of Combat Focus, and the setup is everything: Combat Focus slows time for a short window, so you need five enemies grouped together before you trigger it. The best place to attempt it is a mission or free-roam firefight where enemies cluster — a police roadblock, a gang hideout, or a robbery getaway where the response piles in. Let the enemies gather, wait until at least five are in view and close together, then trigger Combat Focus and work through them with aimed headshots, reloading only if you must. If the focus ends before the fifth takedown, the attempt fails, so do not trigger it early. Group them first, focus second, and the trophy pops on the fifth takedown.
steps: Find a firefight where enemies cluster: a roadblock, hideout, or getaway.
Let at least five enemies gather in view before acting.
Trigger Combat Focus only once five enemies are grouped and close.
Work through them with aimed headshots; do not waste the window.
Take down the fifth enemy inside one focus; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Catch Me If You Can asks you to make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, Vice City International Airport — in plain language, take a plane and take off without a flight plan. The airport is a restricted area, so the first challenge is getting in: drive through a service gate or slip in on foot, then find a plane parked on the tarmac or at a hangar. Once you are in the cockpit, taxi to a runway, throttle up, and lift off — the trophy is about the departure, not the flight, so it should pop as you leave the ground. Expect a wanted level the moment you enter the airport, so go in with a fast approach and do not linger on the tarmac. If you already played the VCIA Takedown story mission, you know the airport's layout, which makes this attempt much easier.
steps: Head to Vice City International Airport and enter via a service gate.
Find a plane parked on the tarmac or at a hangar.
Get in the cockpit and taxi to a runway.
Throttle up and take off — the trophy is about the departure.
Leave the ground unscheduled; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Challenging Tank is the trophy for getting into a Rhino tank and driving it, and the official description's joke — kinda hot in these Rhinos — is the only hint the list gives you. Rhino tanks appear at military locations and in high-wanted-level police responses, so the reliable way to find one is to build a big wanted level in an open area and wait for the military response, or to scout the military base and grab one from its yard. Either way, expect heavy resistance: a tank is not handed over quietly. Once you are in the driver's seat, just drive it — the trophy is about getting in and moving, not about destroying anything. Take it for a short spin down the road and the trophy pops, then enjoy the chaos while it lasts.
steps: Scout a military location or build a high wanted level in an open area.
Wait for a Rhino tank to appear in the response or the yard.
Approach it under cover or during the chaos of the response.
Get into the driver's seat of the Rhino.
Drive the tank; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Sneakthief asks you to rob a jewelry store without being detected, and it is one of the hardest crime trophies because a single spotted moment fails the attempt. The jewelry store has guards and cameras, so the attempt starts before you walk in: scout the store at a quiet hour, learn the guard patrols and the camera angles, and plan your route to the display cases and back out. Move slowly, stay out of sightlines, and take the goods without triggering an alarm — if a guard spots you or a camera catches you, the attempt is over and you start again. A quiet-hour attempt, when the store is nearly empty, is far easier than a busy one. Slip in, take the jewelry, slip out unseen, and the trophy pops.
steps: Scout the jewelry store at a quiet hour; learn guard patrols and camera angles.
Plan a route to the display cases and back out before entering.
Move slowly and stay out of sightlines; avoid guards and cameras.
Take the jewelry without triggering an alarm.
Leave unseen; the trophy pops. If spotted, the attempt fails — retry.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Maximum Withdrawal is the silver trophy for robbing five bank vaults and escaping, and the escape is the hard part — getting into a vault is a plan, getting out with the police on you is a skill. Bank-vault robberies unlock in the later chapters, so do not expect to attempt them early, and each one needs its own plan: scout the bank, know the vault's location and the getaway route, and park a fast car where you can reach it under pressure. Rob the vault, grab the cash, and run the escape route you already planned — improvising a getaway under a full wanted level is how attempts die. Five successful vault jobs is the target, and each one counts the moment you escape clean. Finish the fifth and the silver pops.
steps: Wait until bank-vault robberies unlock in the later chapters.
Scout each bank: vault location, guard positions, getaway route.
Park a fast car on the escape route before starting.
Rob the vault, grab the cash, and run the planned escape.
Escape clean five times; the silver pops after the fifth.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: A Classic Blitz Play asks you to rob an armored truck in free roam and escape, and it is the most accessible robbery trophy on the list — no vault, no crew, just a truck and a getaway. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida, usually with a guard escort, so the attempt starts with finding one: follow the truck until it stops at a delivery point, then hit it fast. Ram it or block it, take the cash from the back, and get out before the police response builds. The escape is the trophy's real test: the moment you grab the cash, the wanted level climbs, so have your getaway car facing the road and your route already in mind. Lose the heat, and the trophy pops the moment you are clear.
steps: Find an armored truck on its route and follow it to a stop.
Block or ram the truck, then take the cash from the back.
Get back to your getaway car fast — the wanted level climbs immediately.
Drive a planned escape route; break line of sight to lose the heat.
Escape clean; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: The Goodtime State asks you to explore all of Leonida, and it is the map-coverage trophy: every named district and area in the state counts, reported as 52 areas in total. The game tracks your exploration in the stats menu, so the first thing to do is open it and see how much of the map the story has already covered for you — the main missions drag you through most of the state's headline locations on their own. What remains is usually the quiet corners: the rural north, the small coastal towns, and the back roads between districts. The efficient route is a road trip, not a checklist: drive the highways and back roads in a fast car, dipping into each named area until the map's fog clears, and let the counter climb. Explore the last area and the trophy pops.
steps: Open the stats menu to see how much of Leonida the story already covered.
Plan a road trip through the areas still unexplored — rural north, coastal towns, back roads.
Drive into each named area until it registers on the map.
Use a fast car and the highways to cover ground quickly.
Explore the final area; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Pest Control asks you to rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang, and it is a tour of Leonida's underworld: every gang runs its own off-the-books operations — stash houses, labs, and cash drops — and you need to hit one of each. The gangs control different districts, so the attempts spread you across the map, and each operation has its own guards and layout, which means scouting before you strike. Hit one operation per gang, take the goods, and get out clean; the game tracks which gangs you have hit, so check the tracker before you plan the next one. You do not need to rob every operation in the game — one per gang is the whole requirement. Hit the last gang's operation and the trophy pops.
steps: Learn which gangs control which districts and where their operations sit.
Scout one operation: guards, entrances, and the escape route.
Rob the operation, take the goods, and escape clean.
Check the tracker for which gangs are still unhit.
Rob the last gang's operation; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description says to enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach, which reads like a simple location activity: a drink at a beachfront bar with the ocean in front of you. The most likely approaches are to visit the beachfront bars along Ocean Beach and order a cocktail at each one, to try the beach bars at different times of day, and to check whether a specific named bar or a particular seat with a sea view is what triggers it. What to try, in order: walk the Ocean Beach strip and enter every beachfront bar, order a drink at the bar, and sit or stand where the ocean is visible. If none of that pops the trophy, the trigger may be tied to a story moment or a specific bar that only opens later — keep the trophy in mind as you play and retry the bars after each chapter.
steps: Walk the Ocean Beach strip and enter every beachfront bar you find.
Order a cocktail at the bar in each one.
Sit or stand where the ocean is visible while you drink.
Try the bars at different times of day if the first attempt fails.
Retry after each story chapter — the trigger may be tied to a later moment.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description says to smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style, which reads like a drive-through-the-window exit from a car dealership. The most likely approaches are to drive a car straight through the showroom's front window from inside, to steal a display car and smash out through the glass with it, and to try the big dealerships in Vice City rather than the small lots. What to try, in order: find a large vehicle showroom with a glass front, get a car inside or steal a display model, then accelerate straight through the window and keep driving. If the glass does not break or the attempt does nothing, try a different showroom or a heavier vehicle — the trigger may be tied to a specific dealership.
steps: Find a large vehicle showroom with a glass front in Vice City.
Get a car inside the showroom or steal a display model.
Accelerate straight through the front window and keep driving.
Try a heavier vehicle if the glass does not break.
Try a different showroom if the first one does nothing.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Let's Go Bowling asks you to play bowling at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley, and the description's word — follow-through — hints at the game's bowling itself: a full game, bowled properly, from the first frame to the last. Head to the Kolt & Associates' alley, pick up a game, and play it through: aim, set your power, and release with a smooth follow-through, frame by frame, until the game ends. You do not need a high score or a strike — finishing the game is what matters — but a steady rhythm helps, and the alley is a relaxed place to practice the timing without pressure. It also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None, and it is worth remembering the alley's location, because the unconfirmed Ten Pin trophy is most likely tied to this same spot.
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Start a game of bowling and play the first frame.
Aim, set power, and release with a smooth follow-through.
Play every frame through to the end of the game.
Finish the game; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description, a partnership with mass appeal, most likely points at a partner-activity milestone: something you do together with your partner that a crowd notices. The candidate approaches are to complete partner activities until a milestone counter fills, to play the partner activities that draw a crowd — races, performances, or public stunts done together — and to keep doing them as a pair rather than solo. What to try, in order: run the partner activities you have unlocked, repeat the ones that visibly draw spectators, and watch for a milestone or a crowd reaction that marks the moment. If nothing pops, the trigger may be a specific partner event later in the story, so keep the trophy in mind and retry partner activities after each chapter.
steps: Unlock partner activities and run them as a pair.
Repeat the activities that visibly draw a crowd or spectators.
Watch for a milestone, a crowd reaction, or a counter filling.
Try races, performances, and public stunts done together.
Retry partner activities after each story chapter if nothing pops.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description, choices made (for better or worse), reads like a story-choice trophy: play the story, make a major decision, and the trophy tracks the choices you make along the way. The candidate approaches are to play the story normally and make the big decisions as they come, to keep a manual save before every major choice so you can see both outcomes, and to watch for a choice counter or a decision log in the stats menu. What to try, in order: make each major story decision when it appears, keep a save before it, and check whether a choice count is rising in the stats. If the trophy needs a specific number of choices, the save-before-every-choice habit is what lets you recover a missed one — and that habit is worth keeping for the whole run anyway.
steps: Play the story and make each major decision as it appears.
Make a manual save before every major story choice.
Check the stats menu for a choice counter or decision log.
If a choice count exists, keep making decisions until it fills.
Keep the save habit for the whole run; the trophy tracks your choices.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description, second time's the charm, reads like a retry after a failure: fail at something, then succeed at the same thing on the next attempt. The candidate approaches are to fail a retryable activity once and then pass it on the immediate second try, to try it on activities with a clear pass-or-fail outcome — a race, a challenge, a fishing attempt — and to attempt it soon after the failure, while the game still remembers the first try. What to try, in order: pick a short activity you can fail quickly, fail it deliberately, then pass it on the very next attempt. If that does nothing, try the same pattern on a different activity — the trigger may be tied to one specific event rather than to retries in general.
steps: Pick a short activity with a clear pass-or-fail outcome (a race, a challenge).
Fail the activity once, deliberately or naturally.
Retry it immediately and pass it on the second attempt.
If nothing pops, try the same pattern on a different activity.
Keep the attempts close together — the trigger likely remembers the first try.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description, what the hell just happened?, reads like a secret encounter or an easter egg: something strange that you stumble into rather than something you plan. The candidate approaches are to explore the strange corners of Leonida — the remote spots, the odd landmarks, and the places that look like they hide something — to visit them at night as well as by day, and to interact with anything unusual you find. What to try, in order: sweep the map's odd landmarks and remote locations, check them at different times of day, and interact with anything that looks out of place. If nothing pops, the trigger may be a random or rare encounter, so keep exploring and let the trophy come to you.
steps: Sweep the map's odd landmarks and remote locations.
Visit them at night as well as by day.
Interact with anything unusual you find.
Check the strange corners: the places that look like they hide something.
Keep exploring; the trigger may be a rare or random encounter.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: This trophy is unconfirmed: no unlock method has been reported yet, so this guide gives you the best reading of the official description and honest candidate approaches — not an invented method. The description, bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by, most likely means a melee attack from a moving vehicle at the bowling alley: a drive-by with a bat or a similar weapon, knocking people over like pins. The candidate approaches are to drive slowly past the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and swing a melee weapon from the vehicle, to try it with a group of pedestrians near the alley's entrance, and to try it at different speeds — slow enough to land the hit, fast enough to count as a drive-by. What to try, in order: get a melee weapon, drive to the bowling alley, and swing from the moving vehicle at people near the entrance. If that does nothing, try it on the alley's parking lot or with a different melee weapon.
steps: Get a melee weapon (a bat or similar) before heading out.
Drive to the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Drive slowly past people near the alley entrance and swing from the vehicle.
Try different speeds: slow enough to hit, fast enough to be a drive-by.
Try the alley parking lot or a different melee weapon if nothing pops.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Dime on the Dollar asks you to earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts, and the total accumulates from robberies and heists across the whole run — you do not need to earn it in one job. Marked bills are the dirty cash that comes out of the big scores, and your contacts clean it for a cut, so the trophy is really about volume: keep robbing, keep heisting, and keep laundering what you earn instead of letting it sit. The contacts who launder for you unlock as the story progresses, and the game tracks the laundered total in its stats, so check it now and then to see how close you are. Bank-vault robberies and armored trucks are the richest source of marked bills, so fold laundering into your crime phase. Reach $250,000 laundered and the trophy pops.
steps: Rob shops, armored trucks, and bank vaults to earn marked bills.
Launder the bills through your contacts as you earn them.
Check the laundered total in the stats menu to track progress.
Prioritize bank vaults and armored trucks — the richest sources.
Reach $250,000 laundered; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Treat Yo Self asks you to spend $100,000 across all shops, and it accumulates all game — every dollar you spend on weapons, ammunition, armor, clothes, cars, and upgrades counts toward the same total. The honest way to earn it is to play normally and spend as you go: the story's missions will have you buying weapons and armor anyway, and a hundred thousand dollars sounds like a lot until you price a good rifle, a full armor set, and a car upgrade. If you reach the cleanup phase and the counter is still short, the fastest way to close the gap is to buy the expensive things you have been postponing — a top-tier weapon, a car, or a full wardrobe — because the total only cares about dollars spent, not what you bought. Reach $100,000 and the trophy pops.
steps: Spend normally as you play: weapons, ammunition, armor, clothes, cars.
Check the spent total in the stats menu to see the gap.
In the cleanup phase, buy the expensive items you postponed.
A top-tier weapon or a car closes a large gap in one purchase.
Reach $100,000 spent; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Little Boxes asks you to purchase all garage properties, reported as eight garages in total, and it is a money trophy in disguise: the garages are expensive, so the real requirement is saving up across the whole run. Garage properties go on sale through the in-game property market, and each one you buy also gives you storage for the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good, so the trophy feeds another trophy as you earn it. The smart route is to buy garages as you can afford them rather than saving for all eight at once — each purchase is progress, and the money you earn from robberies and heists in the crime phase is what funds them. Check the property market regularly for garages you have not bought yet. Buy the eighth and final garage and the trophy pops.
steps: Check the property market for garage properties on sale.
Buy garages as you can afford them; each one is progress.
Use robbery and heist income from the crime phase to fund them.
Garages also store vehicles for Whip It Good — two trophies, one purchase.
Buy the eighth and final garage; the trophy pops.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: On the Spot asks you to register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app, and it is a quick collection trophy once you know the flow: find a vehicle, open the Scooter Bros app, and register it. Any vehicle counts, so the fastest route is to walk a busy street or a parking lot and register the first ten different vehicles you find — parked cars, traffic, anything with wheels. The app tracks which vehicles are registered, so check it if you lose count, and do not register the same vehicle twice: each registration needs a new vehicle. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good, the 100-vehicle discovery trophy, because every vehicle you discover is a vehicle you can register. Register your tenth vehicle and the trophy pops.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app to see the registration flow.
Find a vehicle on a busy street or in a parking lot.
Register it in the app; each vehicle counts once.
Repeat with nine more different vehicles.
Register your tenth vehicle; the trophy pops.
